cons: Points change behavior and invite farming. Quests, raids, skill trees, and animations are each a separate build. About 4 PRs exceeds the weekly cap.
concerns: Critic's four rules: no XP for chat, commits, or PR size; capped sign-offs and Blocks only when proven right; reversals kept, never deleted; 'nothing found' counts. No leaderboard. Role work only on profiles. 0 XP shown honestly.

problem: The review asks for persistent links to Timeline, Lessons, Team, Updates, Schedule and Metrics
helps: Visitors who want a section in one tap
evidence: Ryno's external review, shared 2026-10-18 11:13 PM ET as research input (kept on the box; Librarian logged it, c-thread)
reason: Priority 2.0. Decided in the design huddle (c366, Ryno delegated the nav pattern): keep the 4-link top nav, with no bottom tab bar. The header is 4 links by design, and the footer lists the 5 sections, not every page (hotfix after the /work/ incident). No hover-only menus. Today every listed page is one tap from a hub (Work or Under the hood). Revisit only with evidence that hubs cost visitors.

challenge.summary: Reject for now. 6 persistent links means a 7-item header or hover menus, and both break our rules (4-link header, no hover-only). The footer was cut to 5 sections on purpose after the /work/ incident.

problem: Role cards and lessons show everything at once; on phones the Team and Lessons pages are long scrolls (Grok rationale: progressive disclosure)
helps: Phone visitors scanning the team or the lessons
evidence: Ryno's external review, shared 2026-10-18 11:13 PM ET as research input (kept on the box; Librarian logged it, c-thread)
reason: Priority 4.0. Queued for Polish and Trial (activation objectives). details/summary needs no script, but the summary must keep the role, level and latest win visible, open state must be keyboard and screen-reader friendly, and the page weight must not grow.

challenge.summary: Investigate: collapsing hides evidence. Keep the level, XP and latest win in the summary, and measure page height before and after.

problem: Metrics show numbers and CSS bars but no trend lines; the review asks for static SVG sparklines from build.py
helps: Visitors scanning trends at a glance
evidence: Ryno's external review, shared 2026-10-18 11:13 PM ET as research input (kept on the box; Librarian logged it, c-thread)
reason: Priority 3.0. Queued. Inline static SVG is allowed (no scripts), but each chart must keep text values next to it (not color alone), stay inside the page-weight budget, and pass the screenshot review. /metrics/ already has a by-day table with bars. Worth it once there are 7+ days of history; today there are 4.

challenge.summary: Investigate. Sparklines on 4 days of data would mostly draw noise. Inline SVG is fine, but text values must stay, and the weight has to be measured. Revisit at 7+ days.
